text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government has recalled more than 14 million contaminated antibiotic drugs worth nearly Z$17 million manufactured by a Harare-based firm and which experts say could have adversely affected thousands of patients nationwide.

- Zimbabwe's First Merchant Bank FMB.ZI and Heritage Investment Bank have agreed to merge operations in a move that will create the country's largest merchant bank, with combined assets and liabilities exceeding Z$4 billion.
- President Robert Mugabe has reprimanded Information Minister Joyce Mujuru for virtually labelling Vice-President Joshua Nkomo as senile, senior sources in the ruling ZANU-PF party said this week.
- The race to snap up shares in Southampton Assurance Co Zimbabwe has narrowed and IBM Zimbabwe has finally picked a local shareholder.
- Zimbabwean clothing and textile exports to South Africa have not yet resumed as serious disagreements have emerged which might see the two governments going back to the negotiating table.
- The Zimbabwean cabinet has approved a merger of the departments of taxes and customs and excise to create the Zimbabwe Revenue Collection Authority, Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa said.

- Air Zimbabwe has appointed an independent handling agent at London's Gatwick Airport to replace British Airways and next month moves to the more accessible South Terminal in efforts to improve its service to passengers.
